channel.title: ClarixNews — Latest Articles
channel.description: Latest news, explainers and practical guides from ClarixNews.

item.title: New Technology, Old Questions: What the Federal Reserve Is Actually Asking About AI
item.description: In a November speech, Fed Vice Chair Jefferson placed generative AI inside a century of central-bank experience. The framework he used is the best available guide to how monetary policy will judge the AI boom — and where it could be fooled.

item.title: P97.5 Billion Gone: What the Philippine Senate's DPWH Budget Slash Actually Means
item.description: The Senate cut P97.5 billion from the public works department's 2027 budget. Behind the number sits the Philippines' most consequential annual negotiation — and a simple question: what disappears when roads lose funding?

item.title: The Sandpaper Row Explodes Again: De Villiers Calls Khawaja the 'Biggest Traitor'
item.description: A decade-old scandal found new fuel this week as AB de Villiers' comments about Usman Khawaja reignited cricket's most bitter argument. Here is the backstory, the new claims, and why this wound never healed.

item.title: Why Italy Stops: The Mechanics Behind the November Nationwide Transport Strike
item.description: Italy's transport network went quiet again on November 20–21 as nationwide strikes hit rail, road and air. The frequency is not chaos — it is a legal and institutional machine working exactly as designed.

item.title: Forty-Six Injured in Prague Train Collision: What We Know — and What We Don't Yet
item.description: Two trains collided in the Czech capital, injuring dozens. As with every fast-moving rail incident, the confirmed facts are few and the assumptions are many. Here is the verified picture, and how investigations like this actually proceed.

item.title: The 100,000-Bug Year: A Practical Patch-Triage Playbook for Teams That Can't Fix Everything
item.description: Disclosures doubled this year and AI-assisted patches now cause outages of their own. The winning response is not faster patching — it is better triage. Here is a working playbook, step by step.

item.title: After Akvan: What Actually Happens in the 90 Days Following a Cyclone Landfall
item.description: Landfall makes the headlines; recovery writes the balance sheet. From rescue to relief to reconstruction, here is the machinery that follows a storm — and the three gaps where communities get left behind.

item.title: Hormuz at Nine Months: Why Winter Makes the World's Most Important Closure Harder
item.description: The strait that carried a fifth of the world's oil has been largely shut since February 28. As northern-hemisphere heating season arrives, the closure stops being an oil story and becomes an LNG story — and LNG has no detour.

item.title: The First Post-Ground-Stop Thanksgiving: US Aviation Faces Its Biggest Stress Test of 2026
item.description: Ten days after a four-hour nationwide ground stop cancelled nearly 8,000 flights, the system meets the year's heaviest travel window. The question is not whether planes fly — it is whether slack exists when none is scheduled.

item.title: ANT After the Debut: Five Things the First Weeks of a $1.27 Trillion Stock Will Reveal
item.description: Priced at $83, opened at $111.50, closed 17% up — day one is marketing. The sessions that follow are information. Here is exactly what to watch in Anthropic's first weeks as a public company, and why each signal matters.

item.title: A First in 70 Years: Japan's Forces Will Fire Missiles on Indian Soil
item.description: At the November 19 '2+2' talks, India and Japan signed a letter of intent allowing JSDF live-fire missile training at Indian ranges — a quiet document with a loud message about the Indo-Pacific's new geometry.

item.title: The Machines Stopped: What Bangladesh's Garment Uprising Won — and What It Left Unsettled
item.description: From August street protests to November's factory shutdowns across Ashulia, Gazipur and Dhaka, workers forced a wage reckoning in the industry that clothes the world. Most are back at work — the arithmetic has not changed.

item.title: The AI Trade Melts Down: Dow and S&P 500 Enter Correction as Nasdaq Erases 2026 Gains
item.description: A ~5.3% Nasdaq slide wiped the index's year-to-date gains and pulled the Dow and S&P 500 into correction territory. This is not a rate story — it is an AI-capex story finally meeting arithmetic.

item.title: 100,000 Bugs and Counting: Inside the AI-Driven Vulnerability Flood Reshaping Cybersecurity
item.description: Public vulnerability disclosures passed 100,000 on November 13 — more than double last year's total. AI finds bugs faster than humans can fix them, and the patch queue itself is now causing outages.

item.title: Day 266: What the Strait of Hormuz Closure Is Doing to the World's Oil and LNG
item.description: Two ships transited on November 15 against a normal ~85 a day. Nine months into the closure of the world's most important energy chokepoint, here is what has actually moved — barrels, routes, prices and strategy.

item.title: Two World Cups, One Summer: Cricket and Football Will Collide for 18 Days in 2030
item.description: The FIFA World Cup (June 8–July 21) and the ICC Men's T20 World Cup (July 4–August 4) will overlap for 18 consecutive days — a first in sporting history, and a scheduling earthquake.

item.title: Petrol at Rs323: Pakistan's Quiet Price Squeeze Meets an Export-Led Promise
item.description: OGRA raised petrol by Re1 to Rs323 per litre and held diesel at Rs355 from November 20 — a small move that lands on households already absorbing a 3.65% growth economy.

item.title: Anthropic's $1.27 Trillion Debut: What the Record AI IPO Says About the New Economy
item.description: Priced at $83, opened at $111.50 and closed 17% up on day one — the largest raise in IPO history lands a frontier AI lab on public markets, and raises a governance question nobody has answered.

item.title: Cyclone Akvan Crosses the Andhra Coast: Third Storm in 24 Days Tests India's East Coast
item.description: Three lakh people evacuated and 423 rescue teams staged as Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan makes landfall between Nellore and Visakhapatnam with winds gusting to 110 km/h.

item.title: Four Hours That Stopped a Nation: Inside the 2026 FAA Ground Stop and the Recovery Underway
item.description: Nearly 8,000 cancellations and more than 10,000 delays after US airspace briefly froze. Operations are back — but the episode exposed how thin the margin really is.

item.title: The $19 Trillion Pivot: China's Economy 2000–2026 — From World's Factory to Fortress Economy
item.description: A 26-year economic autopsy of China — WTO accession, the stimulus decade, the COVID exception, and the property hangover. GDP, growth, debt, trade surplus, manufacturing dominance and the demographic cliff, examined through four reference years: 2000, 2010, 2020 and 2026.

item.title: K-Shaped Economy Explained: Why GDP Rises While Your Budget Falls
item.description: The term is everywhere and rarely defined properly. Here is what a K-shaped recovery actually measures, which indicators reveal it, and why averages hide it.

item.title: The 2026 Skills Stack: What Employers Screen For When Every Candidate Has AI
item.description: When everyone can produce a polished draft in thirty seconds, polish stops being a signal. Here is what hiring managers look for instead — and how to demonstrate it.

item.title: Freelancing in Pakistan 2026: The Skills That Pay, Getting Paid Legally, and Keeping Clients
item.description: A practical playbook for earning in dollars — which skills command rates, how payment channels and tax registration work, and why recurring clients beat one-off gigs.

item.title: How to Read a Market Week: Oil, Gold, the Dollar and Bitcoin as One Signal
item.description: Most retail investors watch four charts separately. Professionals read them as a single system. Here is the framework — and what each combination usually means.

item.title: AI Agents in 2026: What They Reliably Do, Where They Fail, and How to Deploy Them Safely
item.description: A practical capability audit — the tasks agents handle end-to-end today, the failure modes that still require humans, and a deployment checklist teams can actually use.

item.title: The $38 Trillion Question: America's Economy 2000–2026 — GDP Tripled, But Who Got Richer?
item.description: A 26-year economic autopsy of the United States — GDP, inflation, poverty, trade deficits, the national debt, and why America can run imbalances that would bankrupt any other nation. An economist's verdict on four reference years: 2000, 2010, 2020, and 2026.

item.title: Pakistan's Economy, 2000–2026: GDP, Inflation, Poverty and the Trade Gap Explained
item.description: A long-run economic review of Pakistan's growth, living standards, exports, imports and trading partners — with clear distinctions between historical observations, fiscal-year data and provisional estimates.

item.title: Bitcoin Tests $85,000 as ETF Inflows and a Quiet Supply Squeeze Collide
item.description: Spot ETFs absorbed $1.4 billion this week, exchange balances sit at seven-year lows, and post-halving issuance keeps shrinking. Traders are calling it the least-loved rally of 2026 — which may be exactly why it keeps working.

item.title: Supreme Court Strikes Down Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Emergency Rule, Orders Provincial Assembly Restored Within 72 Hours
item.description: In a 4-1 ruling, the full bench declares the October 11 proclamation ultra vires — a verdict with immediate political consequences and genuinely difficult security questions amid the ongoing conflict with the Afghan Taliban.

item.title: Four Days Out, Israel's Election Tightens: Netanyahu and Eisenkot Trade Blows in Final Debate as Prediction Markets Reprice
item.description: For the first time since September, money moved toward the incumbent this week. Coalition math still favors a narrow anti-Netanyahu bloc — and everything now turns on turnout models nobody trusts.

item.title: The Man Who Said the Quiet Part: Inside Evan Hubinger's Greater-Than-10-Percent Bet
item.description: Anthropic's alignment science lead publicly agreed that AI 'could kill all humans,' admitted his company has 'no plan to solve alignment for superintelligence' — and then kept going to work. What does it mean to hold that number and still build?

item.title: The Trillion-Dollar Listings: OpenAI and Anthropic File Confidentially for IPOs That Could Dwarf Every Tech Offering in History
item.description: Two labs that spent the summer trading existential-risk warnings are now asking public markets for unprecedented capital. The filings land mid-FRONTIER Act markup — and the risk-factor sections will be unlike anything Wall Street has read.

item.title: From Nobel Stage to Operating Theatre: Optogenetics Begins Its First Human Trials for Inherited Blindness
item.description: Weeks after Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel won the 2026 Medicine prize, two hospitals have enrolled the first patients in light-switch gene therapy trials — the fastest Nobel-to-bedside translation in a decade.

item.title: Pakistan and the Afghan Taliban Sit Down in Doha — First Face-to-Face Talks Since the Airstrikes Began
item.description: Qatari mediators host a technical-level dialogue as strikes continue into a third week. Islamabad wants verifiable action on the TTP; Kabul wants the bombs to stop. Both want the border trade open.

item.title: Brent Crosses $90 for the First Time Since 2024 as OPEC+ Weighs an Emergency Meeting
item.description: Aramco strikes, a ceasefire that may not exist, and thin spare capacity have pushed crude into a pure risk-premium zone. Gold holds near records; Pakistan's import bill quietly grows by billions.

item.title: Recursive Self-Improvement, Explained: The AI Idea Behind the Anthropic Resignation Storm
item.description: When Jacob Coxon warned that labs are 'racing straight to self-improving superintelligence,' what exactly did he mean? A plain-English guide to RSI — and why serious experts still disagree about it.

item.title: iPhone Duo First Reviews Are In: 'The Crease Is Gone' — But Is $1,999 Too Much?
item.description: Review embargoes lifted 24 hours before the foldable goes on sale. Critics agree on the hinge, the battery and the display. They disagree, sharply, on everything the price implies.

item.title: The 'Coxon Effect': How One Resignation Thread Pushed the FRONTIER Act From Proposal to Senate Markup
item.description: Six weeks after Jacob Coxon's viral warning — and with Evan Hubinger's >10% extinction-risk claim on the record — lawmakers cite the thread in hearings as the bipartisan AI bill gains real momentum.

item.title: Pakistan Supreme Court Hears Challenges to Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Emergency Rule — Verdict Expected This Week
item.description: As protests continue and the conflict with the Afghan Taliban persists, a full bench weighs whether Articles 232 and 234 were constitutionally invoked — a decision that could redefine federal-provincial relations.

item.title: Hurricane Isaias Aftermath: FEMA Mobilizes as the Southeast Counts the Cost of 2026's Strongest Storm
item.description: Category 3 landfall left millions without power and early insured losses estimated at $8–12 billion. Federal response speed is under scrutiny after last season's delays.

item.title: US Midterms 2026: Control of Congress Goes to the Voters as the Trump Era Faces Its First Referendum
item.description: With Election Day on November 3, narrow House margins, a razor-thin Senate, and an economy-and-AI ballot make 2026 one of the most consequential midterms in a generation.

item.title: One Week After Lung Surgery, Pope Leo XIV Appears at Gemelli Hospital Window to Bless Crowds
item.description: The pontiff's brief appearance — pale but smiling — ends days of global concern. Vatican confirms recovery is 'on track' and a return to the Vatican is expected within weeks.

item.title: How to Build an AI Career in 2026: Skills, Projects, Portfolio and a Realistic 90-Day Roadmap
item.description: A practical guide for students and career changers to move beyond AI hype, learn job-ready fundamentals, build credible projects and apply for entry-level opportunities.

item.title: Opinion: AI Should Make People More Capable, Not More Dependent
item.description: The real test of artificial intelligence is not how much work it can generate, but whether people can use it to think more clearly, make better decisions and retain control.

item.title: AI Stock Market Boom Faces a Reality Check: Why Investors Are Questioning Big Tech's Trillion-Dollar Spending
item.description: A sharp Nasdaq pullback, rising scrutiny of data-centre spending and uncertain returns are forcing investors to ask whether AI profits can catch up with AI investment.

item.title: Asian Stock Markets Slide as Oil Prices Rise and AI Earnings Put Investors on Edge
item.description: South Korean and regional shares weaken amid geopolitical pressure, higher crude prices and a crucial week for major technology-company earnings.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang Urges German Industry to Embrace AI: What It Means for Manufacturing and Jobs
item.description: As AI moves beyond chatbots into robotics, vehicles and factory systems, Germany's industrial base faces a strategic choice: build local capability or depend heavily on outside technology.

item.title: One Month After the Viral Warning: What Has — and Hasn't — Changed at Anthropic and in AI Policy
item.description: Jacob Coxon's resignation thread reached 115 million people. Thirty days on, we track the FRONTIER Act's momentum, Evan Hubinger's >10% extinction-risk claim, and what new data says about self-improving AI.

item.title: Oil on Edge: Brent Pushes Toward $90 as Yemen Strikes and Energy-Ceasefire Confusion Rattle Markets
item.description: Aramco facilities hit by Houthi strikes, Ukraine disputes Trump's ceasefire claim, and gold holds above $4,100 — here's the complete investor picture for the week.
